findings.F1: The backtest holds only BTCUSD in a single window w1 of 120 daily bars (119 days), not the brief's three coins. That gives only 23 non-overlapping 5-bar blocks in total, so even if every block were extreme it could not reach the plan's minimum of 30 cases.
findings.F2: The forecast reached −10 or lower on 15 of 120 bars (12.5%), grouped into 3 episodes, which left only 3 grid cases against the 30 required. At that share, 30 non-overlapping cases would need about 1200 daily bars per coin, roughly 3.3 years.
findings.F3: The component's logged RSI never exceeded 58.0 (median 47.5, 95th percentile 55.2, 0 bars above 60 or 70), and the bars with forecast ≤ −10 had RSI between 54.0 and 58.0 (mean 55.6). The "high extreme" was therefore only high relative to the 60-bar standardisation, not an absolute extreme. A Wilder RSI(14) recomputed on the closes ranged from 11.9 to 70.1.
findings.F4: The direction leaned towards reversal but was underpowered. The 3 grid cases had excess 5-bar returns of −13.3%, −0.7% and −6.3% (mean −6.75%, t −1.84). The 15 overlapping extreme bars averaged −2.3% (std 5.7%, t −1.60), and about 23 independent cases would give t = −2 at that effect size, because the 5-bar forward return std is 7.3%.
findings.F5: The excess return deepened as the forecast grew more negative: −1.3% (t −1.15, n 39) for any short reading, −1.6% (t −1.33) at ≤ −1, −2.7% (t −1.73, n 23) at ≤ −5. This happened in a window where BTC fell 21.1% and the 5-bar baseline was −0.5%.

ideas.idea: When a coin's RSI(14) on daily bars is high relative to its own previous 60 readings, its return over the next 5 bars is below its average 5-bar return, observed on each of BTC, ETH and BNB over several years of daily bars.
ideas.consequence: A trader could short, or refuse longs, when daily RSI is high against its recent range, once enough independent cases exist to judge the edge.
ideas.name: relative-high RSI daily reversal
ideas.data: instruments: BTC, ETH, BNB; bar: 1d; period: 2018 to 2024, all available windows

ideas.idea: When a coin's RSI(14) on 4-hour bars is high relative to its own previous 60 readings, its return over the next 5 bars is below its average 5-bar return.
ideas.consequence: At the 4-hour scale a trader gets six times as many bars per period, so the reversal after high RSI readings can be traded and checked within a single year.
